findings.title: Live disposition scenario still enumerates review-external as currently generated and architect as the 16th workflow
findings.recommendation: The 'Generated-file disposition' requirement's 'Orbit-authored — full ownership' scenario says 'currently ... the net-new editorial workflows — review, audit-drift, review-external, address-reviews ... and orbit-architect, the fully orbit-authored 16th workflow'. Post-archive the review-external template retires (16 → 15), so this live current-state enumeration contradicts the merged surface. The delta already touches orbit-conventions but not this requirement, and at-archive note 9.4 covers only the two Purpose paragraphs. Add a MODIFIED block for this requirement (drop review-external from the 'currently' list, re-anchor the workflow count) or extend note 9.4's sweep to name it.

findings.title: Baseline 'Architect workflow available' still states 'the generated surface grows to 16 workflows'
findings.recommendation: The parenthetical '(D15 full surface — the generated surface grows to 16 workflows)' is part of a live requirement statement and will contradict the post-archive 15-workflow surface. The architect delta modifies only the emit requirement, and no at-archive note covers this spot. Add a MODIFIED block (or fold into a baseline-sweep at-archive note) rephrasing the count as historical ('grew the surface to 16 at D2; 15 post-D5's merge') or dropping the number.

findings.title: Membership criterion for open_questions_with_recommendation is undefined
findings.recommendation: The counter grammar defines how ENTRIES are counted (top-level list items, fence-aware) but never states what makes an entry count as 'with recommendation': whether the literal `Standing recommendation: none yet` counts, and whether the slot line must appear within the entry's nested content. The scenario ('2 open questions, 1 carrying a standing recommendation → "1 of 2"') doesn't disambiguate, and the conventions delta's 'the slot is what the emit surface's attestation counts' (orbit-conventions delta line 155) reads as slot-presence counting — two implementers would fork. State the criterion in the computed-extensions requirement.

recommendation_options.label: Count real leanings only
recommendation_options.body: An entry counts toward n when its content carries a `Standing recommendation:` line whose value is NOT the literal `none yet` — the attestation measures recorded leanings (the leak-hardening intent); slot-less entries and `none yet` entries both fall outside n, and audit-drift separately flags slot-less entries as format violations.

recommendation_options.label: Count slot presence
recommendation_options.body: An entry counts toward n when a `Standing recommendation:` line is present regardless of value — the attestation measures format compliance (matching the conventions delta's 'the slot is what the attestation counts' phrasing); adjust the audit-drift cross-check prose to match.

findings.title: Task 3.1 and design D1's usage line omit the --doc flag the spec requires
findings.recommendation: The emit-composition spine requirement defines a target-resolution contract where architecture-scoped commands take `--doc <doc-name>` INSTEAD of `--change` (with mutual-exclusion usage errors), and the write-gate scenario invokes `orbit emit review --doc my-program` — but task 3.1's CLI flag list names only `--change`, `--payload`, `--json`, `--render`, and design.md line 13's usage synopsis likewise shows no `--doc`. Add `--doc` (and the exclusion errors) to task 3.1 and the design D1 synopsis so the CLI registration task covers the architecture-scoped channel.

findings.title: Archived-trail resolution for orbit emit archive is unstated
findings.recommendation: `orbit emit archive --change foo` must write to `orbit/changes/archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>-foo/.orbit-runs/` after the move, but how the surface resolves the date prefix from `--change foo` is unspecified (today's UTC date vs. scanning for the matching archive directory — these diverge when the emit fires across a UTC midnight from the move, or when multiple archives share the name stem). State the rule, e.g. the lexically greatest `orbit/changes/archive/*-<name>/` directory, with the existing clean not-found error when none matches.

findings.title: Payload-channel error paths (no payload; both channels) unspecified
findings.recommendation: The payload contract specifies stdin-or-`--payload` and rejects bad keys, but not the behavior when no payload is supplied at all (empty stdin, no flag) or when both `--payload` and stdin are provided. One sentence closes it: absent payload = clean non-zero error naming the channel; both supplied = `--payload` wins (or a usage error) — keeping the no-file/empty-stdout guarantee.

findings.title: 'Review mode decision framework' still calls reviewer classes 'modes' post-merge
findings.recommendation: The delta-modified requirement keeps 'choosing among orbit's three review modes (in-context, `--fresh`, external)' while the same change installs 'the same three-class vocabulary' (`--reviewer`, `reviewer_class`, cadence slots) and reserves 'mode' for `--as proposal|system|architecture` on the merged surface. Rewording the requirement's frame to 'three reviewer classes' (keeping the requirement title stable if renaming is unwanted) would remove the last vocabulary overload the merge otherwise resolves.

commentary: Three iterations of resolution have pushed the residue to the outermost ring: everything inside the delta set now holds together under fairly aggressive probing. I diffed all 23 MODIFIED blocks mechanically against their baseline requirements (no dropped scenarios, no silent content loss — every diff is the intended edit plus additive scenarios), verified the gates.ts :77/:397 line claims and the two render sites against source, checked the inventory's 40.6k/9.8k/8.3k figures against sketches/body-inventory.md, confirmed strict validation, 23/23 fingerprints, and the 0/30 gate arithmetic, and swept baseline specs, README, CLAUDE.md, and src/ for the retired invocation. What remains splits into two textures: (1) live baseline blocks OUTSIDE the delta set that carry current-state surface enumerations — the conventions disposition table and architect's 16-workflow parenthetical — the exact class the at-archive notes exist for but don't yet cover; and (2) small determinism gaps in the new grammars where two implementers could fork (the attestation's membership criterion being the one with real behavioral consequence, since audit-drift cross-checks the recorded value against a fresh parse — a criterion mismatch between the two implementations would manufacture false WARNING drift). The frozen-record vocabulary discipline is applied consistently throughout; I found no place where the merge leaks into record shapes, and no marker residue anywhere in the change directory.
